summary: This is a Makefile snippet that checks the PHP version being used and prints an appropriate message to the console. If PHP 8 or higher is set, it tells the user to upgrade dependencies; otherwise, it says to downgrade to PHP 7. The message is printed in bold yellow text.

explanations.2: This uses shell arithmetic to compare SET_PHP_VERSION against 8. The 'expr' command evaluates the comparison (\>= means 'greater than or equal to'), and ifeq checks if the result equals 1 (true).
explanations.3: The @printf command prints colored text to the console. The \e[1;${COLOR_YELLOW}m codes are ANSI escape sequences that make the text bold and yellow, and \e[0m resets the formatting back to normal.
explanations.5: This is the fallback message printed if the PHP version is less than 8, using the same colored formatting as line 3.
